title: Iron Man
whyItMatters: The film that built the face Doomsday now wears, establishing the armoured-genius archetype the Multiverse Saga keeps reflecting back at us. Watching it first makes the casting echo behind Doctor Doom land far harder.

title: The Incredible Hulk
whyItMatters: Banner's first MCU outing and the origin of the Abomination, who returns decades later. Optional, but it is the only place the early gamma story is told.

title: Iron Man 2
whyItMatters: Introduces Black Widow and War Machine and widens Stark's world into a shared universe. Light prep, but the Stark legacy is what Doom's casting plays against.

title: Thor
whyItMatters: Establishes Asgard, the Bifrost and the brothers whose rivalry runs through the whole saga. It is where Loki's grievance begins.

title: Captain America: The First Avenger
whyItMatters: Steve Rogers, the serum and the Tesseract — the object that starts the cosmic thread. It also sets up the friendship that defines Bucky's arc.

title: The Avengers
whyItMatters: The original assembly that defines what the word 'Avengers' is supposed to mean before Doomsday redefines it. It also plants the Battle of New York, the exact timeline knot that later branches the Sacred Timeline apart.

title: Iron Man 3
whyItMatters: Stark's post-New York trauma and the first fake Mandarin, a thread Shang-Chi later picks up. Optional for Doomsday, essential for the Stark arc.

title: Thor: The Dark World
whyItMatters: Introduces the Aether and the Convergence, the saga's first look at realities bleeding together. It is also where Loki first fakes his own ending.

title: Captain America: The Winter Soldier
whyItMatters: HYDRA hollows out SHIELD from the inside and Bucky comes back as a weapon. The trust it destroys never fully returns to the team.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy
whyItMatters: Opens the cosmic side of the MCU and introduces the Infinity Stones as objects with rules. Essential context for how big the board actually is.

title: Avengers: Age of Ultron
whyItMatters: Introduces Wanda Maximoff, whose reality-warping becomes the hinge of every multiversal crisis that follows. It is also the first time the team is broken from inside rather than outside.

title: Ant-Man
whyItMatters: Introduces Pym Particles and the Quantum Realm — the doorway that later makes the time heist possible. Small film, enormous consequences.

title: Captain America: Civil War
whyItMatters: Establishes the fracture lines and personal grudges that Doomsday's enormous ensemble will be forced to reconcile. It is also the clearest statement of why heroes lose to each other long before they lose to a villain.

title: Doctor Strange
whyItMatters: Your primer on the Multiverse itself: dimensions, mirror realities and the rules Doomsday is about to break. Strange's arrogance here is the same arrogance that will cost the 616 dearly.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2
whyItMatters: Ego establishes that Celestial-scale beings walk among the living. It also cements the found-family core the cosmic tier runs on.

title: Spider-Man: Homecoming
whyItMatters: Peter's first solo outing and the mentor relationship that defines his losses. Everything No Way Home takes away, this film builds.

title: Thor: Ragnarok
whyItMatters: Strips Thor down to the last Asgardian and sets his standing in the Doomsday line-up. It also closes the loop on Loki's loyalties right before the timeline splits him in two.

title: Black Panther
whyItMatters: Wakanda is one of the few powers on Earth able to answer an Incursion-level threat, and this is its foundation. Shuri's arc starts here and ends up on the Doomsday board.

title: Avengers: Infinity War
whyItMatters: The benchmark for what a single villain can cost the universe, and the bar Doom is written to clear. Every alliance Doomsday tests was forged or shattered in these two films.

title: Ant-Man and the Wasp
whyItMatters: Deepens the Quantum Realm and introduces Ghost, who resurfaces on the Thunderbolts roster. The post-credits scene ties it straight to Infinity War.

title: Captain Marvel
whyItMatters: Introduces the most powerful hero on Earth's rolodex and the cosmic politics she polices. When reality starts collapsing, Carol is the first call anyone makes.

title: Avengers: Endgame
whyItMatters: The time heist is the original sin of the Multiverse Saga: branched realities created and abandoned in the name of saving one. Doomsday is, in the plainest terms, the bill arriving for that choice.

title: Spider-Man: Far From Home
whyItMatters: Introduces the idea of a 'multiverse' to the public as a lie before it becomes the truth. It also leaves Peter in the exact position that forces him to ask Strange for the spell.

title: WandaVision
whyItMatters: Wanda's grief becomes the most dangerous force on Earth and sets her on the path to the Darkhold. It also delivers the first real mutant-adjacent misdirection of the saga.

title: The Falcon and the Winter Soldier
whyItMatters: Hands the shield to Sam Wilson, the Captain America who will be standing at the front of the Doomsday roster. It also introduces John Walker, now a Thunderbolt with a grudge.

title: Loki — Season 1
whyItMatters: The single most important text in the saga: it explains the Sacred Timeline, the TVA, branching and what pruning costs. Nothing about an Incursion makes sense without it.

title: Black Widow
whyItMatters: Introduces Yelena, Red Guardian and Taskmaster — three-fifths of the team now branded as Earth's Avengers. It is the Thunderbolts' real origin story.

title: What If...? — Season 1
whyItMatters: The clearest illustration of how small divergences produce wildly different variants of familiar heroes. It teaches the visual grammar Doomsday's variant cast will rely on.

title: Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings
whyItMatters: Adds a mystical power source older than the Avengers and a hero already being scouted for the next team. The Ten Rings' signal in the finale is still an open thread heading into Doomsday.

title: Eternals
whyItMatters: Reveals the Celestial machinery underneath Earth and the beings who out-scale every Avenger. It is the closest the 616 has come to a Galactus-tier threat before First Steps.

title: Hawkeye
whyItMatters: Establishes the street-level bench of the next Avengers and Clint's reluctant mentor role. It also introduces Yelena Belova's grudge, which carries straight into the Thunderbolts.

title: Moon Knight
whyItMatters: Widens the board to gods and afterlives — powers that operate outside the TVA's paperwork. Marc Spector is exactly the kind of unaffiliated asset a war for reality drags in.

title: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness
whyItMatters: The film that names Incursions on screen and shows a dead universe consumed by one. It also debuts America Chavez, the Illuminati and the mutants standing on the far side of the wall.

title: Ms. Marvel
whyItMatters: Quietly drops the word 'mutation' into the 616 for the first time, opening the door the X-Men will walk through. Kamala's ClanDestine arc also plays with dimensional travel.

title: Thor: Love and Thunder
whyItMatters: Gorr proves gods can be killed and leaves Thor with something to protect. It sets his state of mind heading into the next assembly.

title: She-Hulk: Attorney at Law
whyItMatters: Re-establishes the Hulk bloodline and the legal-civilian texture of a superhero Earth. It also returns Daredevil to the board ahead of his Doomsday-era role.

title: Werewolf by Night
whyItMatters: A one-hour special that opens the monster corner of the MCU. Short, optional, and the fastest way to meet a tier Doomsday may well need.

title: Black Panther: Wakanda Forever
whyItMatters: Puts Shuri in the mantle and Namor's Talokan on the geopolitical map as a second unaligned superpower. Both are pieces the Doomsday conflict cannot ignore.

title: The Guardians of the Galaxy Holiday Special
whyItMatters: A 44-minute cosmic breather that sets up the Guardians' final chapter. Pure optional fun.

title: Spider-Man: No Way Home
whyItMatters: The first time the MCU physically pulls people across universes and shows what it costs to send them back. It is the proof of concept for everything Doomsday attempts at scale.

title: Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania
whyItMatters: Shows the Quantum Realm as a doorway between realities and the scale of a multiversal war council. Scott Lang's ordinary-guy stakes are the emotional yardstick Doomsday will use.

title: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3
whyItMatters: Clears the cosmic table and explains why certain heroes are off-world when Earth's sky tears open. It also closes the Guardians roster that Doomsday inherits.

title: Secret Invasion
whyItMatters: Establishes that Earth's defences can be compromised from the inside without a single punch thrown. It also reshapes Nick Fury's standing right before the biggest assembly of his career.

title: Loki — Season 2
whyItMatters: Resolves who is holding the timeline together and at what personal cost, which is the precondition for every Incursion to come. This is the closest the saga has to a rulebook for Doomsday.

title: The Marvels
whyItMatters: Punches a literal hole between realities and lands one of its heroes somewhere very familiar to X-Men fans. That mid-credits moment is a load-bearing beam of the Incursion storyline.

title: What If...? — Season 2
whyItMatters: More divergences, more variants, and a clearer picture of how the Watcher's multiverse behaves. Named an essential on most 2026 prep guides.

title: Echo
whyItMatters: Grounds the ancestral-power side of the MCU and keeps the Kingpin/Daredevil thread alive. It is optional prep, but it explains where the New York street tier stands.

title: Deadpool & Wolverine
whyItMatters: Canonises the Fox universe as a real, dying timeline and explains anchor beings, the Void and how variants get salvaged. It is the bridge that lets legacy mutants stand in a Doomsday line-up at all.

title: What If...? — Season 3
whyItMatters: Closes the animated multiverse anthology and pushes its variants toward a crossover of their own. Useful grounding for how variants get recruited.

title: Agatha All Along
whyItMatters: Keeps the magical tier warm and moves the Maximoff bloodline forward while Wanda is off the board. Useful context for anyone tracking who can still bend reality.

title: Captain America: Brave New World
whyItMatters: Sets Sam Wilson's Captain America against a hostile White House and a world with no Avengers to call. That political vacuum is exactly what Doom will walk into.

title: Daredevil: Born Again
whyItMatters: Restores Matt Murdock as a frontline defender of New York under an authoritarian city hall. Doomsday's ground war needs someone holding Hell's Kitchen.

title: Thunderbolts*
whyItMatters: Assembles the disposable, government-branded team that the world is calling its Avengers when Doomsday begins. It also introduces the single most dangerous power level currently walking the 616.

title: Ironheart
whyItMatters: Riri Williams builds the next generation of powered armour while magic pulls at her from the other side. She is one of the young heroes inheriting the board.

title: Eyes of Wakanda
whyItMatters: A four-part animated anthology on Wakanda's history and its vibranium artefacts across centuries. Optional, but it deepens the one nation that can answer a global threat.

title: Marvel Zombies
whyItMatters: A What If...? spin-off that takes one branch of the multiverse to its horror conclusion. It shows what an unchecked reality actually costs.

title: Wonder Man
whyItMatters: Simon Williams' Hollywood story sits at the seam between celebrity and superheroics. He is a comics Avenger being placed on the board now.

title: The Fantastic Four: First Steps
whyItMatters: Introduces Marvel's First Family and the retro-futurist universe they call home, along with the cosmic scale of Galactus. Doomsday is, at heart, a Fantastic Four story — this is chapter one.

title: Daredevil: Born Again — Season 2
whyItMatters: Matt Murdock's fight for New York escalates as Fisk tightens his grip on the city. It sets the ground-level stakes Doomsday will disrupt.

title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day
whyItMatters: Peter Parker's first outing after the spell, rebuilding a life nobody remembers. It is the last check-in with him before the biggest crossover since Endgame.

title: VisionQuest
whyItMatters: The final chapter of the WandaVision trilogy, following White Vision's search for who he was. It lands two months before Doomsday and closes the saga's synthezoid thread.

title: X-Men
whyItMatters: The origin point of the legacy mutant timeline whose survivors keep reappearing in the MCU. Meet Xavier, Magneto and Wolverine as the 616 will inherit them.

title: X2: X-Men United
whyItMatters: The high-water mark of the original team and the definitive statement of Xavier's dream. It frames the sacrifice logic that legacy mutants bring into an Incursion.

title: X-Men: First Class
whyItMatters: Rebuilds Xavier and Magneto's friendship from the ground up and gives you the second face each actor wears. Essential if you want the returning cast's history to make sense.

title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
whyItMatters: The Fox saga's own timeline-rewrite story, and the template for how a franchise erases and restores its cast. Read it as the dress rehearsal for what Doomsday does across studios.

title: Deadpool
whyItMatters: Establishes Wade Wilson's voice, healing factor and fourth-wall awareness — the reason he can narrate a multiversal crisis. Light prep, but it makes his MCU crossing far funnier.

title: Deadpool 2
whyItMatters: Adds time travel and the X-Force bench to Wade's toolkit and ends on a timeline edit of its own. It sets up the exact status quo Deadpool & Wolverine picks apart.

title: Logan
whyItMatters: The elegy for the original Wolverine and Xavier, and the emotional weight every legacy-mutant return now carries. Watch it before any reunion so you know what is being undone.
